articles.title: Download mode explained: how to enter it, what each screen means, and how to exit safely
articles.excerpt: If you have ever plugged a Samsung phone into a flashing tool and watched it sit there unrecognized, Download mode is usually the missing piece. It is a low-level state that lets a computer talk to th…
articles.body: If you have ever plugged a Samsung phone into a flashing tool and watched it sit there unrecognized, Download mode is usually the missing piece. It is a low-level state that lets a computer talk to the phone before the normal system starts. That is why tools such as Odin need it: they are not installing an app, they are writing system software, and they need a stable channel to do that work. What Download mode actually does Download mode, also called Odin mode, puts the phone in a waiting state. The phone is not booting into its home screen, and it is not running your apps. Instead, it listens for instructions over USB and accepts a firmware package when a trusted tool sends one.
articles.author: SamFware

articles.title: What We Learned Building Cross-Channel Message Routing
articles.excerpt: What We Learned Building Cross-Channel Message Routing for Chatbots Sooner or later, every chatbot project hits the same wall: customers don't stay on one channel. A user asks a question on Instagram,…
articles.body: What We Learned Building Cross-Channel Message Routing for Chatbots Sooner or later, every chatbot project hits the same wall: customers don't stay on one channel. A user asks a question on Instagram, follows up on WhatsApp, and expects the Telegram bot to know what happened. If each channel runs its own isolated logic, you end up with duplicated flows, lost context, and replies that arrive twice or not at all. This is a behind-the-scenes post about how we approached cross-channel message routing for chatbots , the mistakes we made, and the patterns that held up. By the end you'll know how to design a normalized message format, build channel adapters, route messages reliably, and avoid the failure modes that cost us the most time.

The demo company is BharatBiz, a fictional small business based in Bengaluru. The user starts by loading outward-sales invoice PDFs. GST Helper reads the invoices, extracts values, shows page evidence, and turns the documents into a guided GSTR-1 review flow. The current app prepares these GSTR-1 sections: Table 4A regular domestic B2B invoices Table 12 B2B HSN/SAC summary Table 13 document numbers issued It shows the invoice value including tax, taxable value, IGST, CGST, SGST or UTGST, cess, total tax, and invoice count for the supported B2B scope.

articles.body: Part 6 of a series. Previously: Part 5 — Distributing the Workers and the Memory Budget . Part 5 ended with the 77 GB coordinator finally running as it should — resident, no thrashing, the memory problem resolved by moving the workers to a second machine. That made it possible to answer a question Part 4 had deferred: now that the big model can actually run, does a bigger coordinator fix orchestration? The answer was no, and the reason reshaped how the team was run. The ceiling persists on the big model With memory no longer the bottleneck, the coordinator's orchestration could be judged on its own merits. It sequenced delegations more reliably than Gemma had — but it did not escape the same failure modes.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 17, 2016: Private Antares rocket returns to flight after catastrophic launch explosion
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 17, 2016, the Antares rocket now built by Northrop Grumman Space Systems returned to flight to come back from a catastrophic explosion. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems ) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch. The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. Six days later, the Cygnus cargo spacecraft arrived at the ISS to deliver food, supplies and science experiments to the crew.

articles.body: Autonomous agents are the hottest thing in AI. OpenAI, Meta, Google, Instinct, and others promise their agents can scour the internet on your behalf, doing anything from booking a dinner reservation and cleaning out your inbox to buying new shoes. But what happens when the rest of the internet won't play nice? In recent weeks, users of services like Meta's Muse, xAI's Grok, OpenAI's Dots, and Instinct have reported blocks preventing their AI agents from performing tasks across top websites. articles.title: 'Lanterns' shocking finale left us with a lot of unanswered questions for a potential season 2
articles.excerpt: John Stewart goes rogue in Sector 2814 and embraces fear hopefully leading into season 2
articles.body: HBO and HBO Max's " Lanterns " served up its big cliffhanger finale on Oct. 4, 2026, and we’ve been slowly digesting thoughts on what the creative direction and ultimate legacy of this debut season were. While by no means a perfect experiment in trying to shake up the aging superhero genre, there are enough worthy elements to consider this sci-fi mystery show an evolutionary step towards the next generation of comic-based storytelling. After the emerald-tinted dust has settled, there are many lingering questions about where this acclaimed series from creators Chris Mundy, Damon Lindelof, and Tom King might be headed and where the twists and turns might lead for a sophomore season should it be greenlit (get it?) for a triumphant return.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
